question: After 1500 cycles, what capacity does the cathode deliver per gram of sulfur and per gram of the whole electrode, and what sulfur share of the electrode does their ratio imply, against the sulfur content the paper states?

trace.query: SELECT id, page, text FROM lines WHERE id IN ('p5.L104','p5.L101','p5.L105','p5.L102','p5.L103') OR text ILIKE '%306 mAh%' OR text ILIKE '%87 mAh%' OR text ILIKE '%35 wt%' ORDER BY page, line_no

SELECT 100.0 * CAST(regexp_extract((SELECT text FROM lines WHERE id='p5.L105'),'([0-9]+) mAh/g',1) AS DOUBLE) / CAST(regexp_extract((SELECT text FROM lines WHERE id='p5.L103'),'([0-9]+) mAh/',1) AS DOUBLE) AS implied_share_pct

door_refusals.why: a SELECT without FROM reads no atom, so its value has no source

door_refusals.why: fmt pct1 shows a fraction as a percent by multiplying it by 100, and this sql already multiplies by 100: the answer would show 2,843.1% where the value is 28.4%
moves: keep the * 100 and use fmt fixed1 (the value is already in percent; write % in your words after it)
or drop the * 100 and keep fmt pct1

rendered: Per gram of sulfur, the cathode delivers 306 mAh[1] at the end of the long-cycling test (per gram of sulfur). Per gram of the whole electrode, it delivers 87 mAh/g[2] after the same cycling. Dividing the electrode-based value by the sulfur-based value gives an implied sulfur share of about 28.4[3] % of the electrode mass. This is lower than the sulfur content the paper states: the paper describes the moderate loading as 35 wt % active sulfur[4], so the implied share falls short of the stated value by several percentage points.
